title: Is Micron No Longer a Cyclical Business? | MU Stock Deep Dive Part 2
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Part 2 of the Micron deep dive tackles management's claim that Micron is no longer a cyclical business. The market still prices it as one: forward P/E sits in the mid-single digits. But management is pushing a re-rating argument built on 26 strategic long-term take-or-pay customer agreements stretching to 2030–2031, covering 35%+ of revenue with price floors. Parkevtate walks through why the agreements genuinely help — demand visibility lets Micron plan supply, manufacturing and R&D with less variability — but concludes the right question is not 'cyclical or not' but 'how cyclical'. His answer: still a cyclical business, just less cyclical and with a longer, shallower cycle. A true re-rating would need the multiple to widen off the ~5.8x forward P/E. No explicit call in this part — the final verdict is reserved for Part 4, which remains members-only. Other tickers: none discussed beyond passing comparables. Note: captions were auto-generated and garbled some technical terms; the key figures (26 agreements, 35%+ of revenue, mid-single-digit forward P/E) were cross-checked against the slide-style cadence of the narration.
